Get Living: website improvement prototypes

Five greyscale, clickable prototypes for improvements to getliving.com, prepared by ClerksWell. They are about content, layout and how things work. Colour, type and imagery come in the next phase.

Version V1 28 September 2026 Status: internal review Sample data

Prototypes

  • 1. Find a home R10–R17

    Sticky filters, list and map views, cards with the facts renters compare, save and compare homes, search alerts and a waitlist.

  • 2. Property page R20–R27

    Key facts beside the photos, an estimate of monthly costs, a move-in cost breakdown, getting around, and similar homes.

  • 3. Book a viewing R30–R32, R34

    Three steps: how to view, day and time, your details. With the shortened enquiry form (R33) alongside.

  • 4. Renting with us R40–R44

    Rewritten for the Renters' Rights Act: plain-English explainer, how renting works, a comparison with a typical private let, and reviews.

  • 5. Neighbourhood template R50–R56

    One structure for all six neighbourhoods, shown with Sherlock Quarter: live availability and prices, map layers, commute, reviews, events and FAQs.

Modules

  • Module library

    The new reusable components used across the five prototypes, each shown once.

Suggested route through

  • Start at Find a home. Filter to Birmingham, save a couple of homes, tick Compare on two or three and open the comparison. Switch to Map.

  • Open a home. Change the number of people in "What it costs each month" and switch the deposit option. Then Book a viewing and go through all three steps.

  • Open Renting with us, then a neighbourhood from the Locations menu. Toggle the map layers.

How to review this

  • Annotations are hidden to start with. Use "Show annotations" at the bottom right of any page: yellow notes explain behaviour a screenshot can't show; red notes are questions for Get Living.

  • Filters, map pins, save, compare, alerts, the cost estimator, the booking steps, forms, tabs, accordions and carousels all work. Links to pages outside these five go nowhere by design.

  • Listings are sample data. Neighbourhood and building names and rent levels follow the live site; sizes, floors, dates and offers are invented.

  • Resize the browser or open on a phone to check the mobile layouts.
